main_text.l: probatur exemplis, qui se Imperiò sponte abdicarunt.
3. Regnum virtute patandum[?]. Quia Regnum male quaesitum, justè administrari nequit: Regnum scelere partum, minimè est diu-turnum: Tyrannidem occupatium mors plerum-que cruenta.
4. Regnum absque gravissimâ causâ à stirpe non amovendum.
Agitur hîc de electionis & successionis commodis atque incommodis.
5. Ad regni successionem imperiiq; majestatem non temerè admittenda foemina.
6. Difficile peregrinum imperium. Probatur hoc à variis incommodis; ex Principum peregrinorum imperio emergentibus.
7. Facilius est regnum occupare, quàm retinere.
8. Imperium facile iis retinetur artibus, quibus initio partum.

page.notes: Printed word "patandum" in thesis 3 is doubtful: it may be "parandum"; marked [?]. Punctuation after "incommodis" in thesis 6 and after "adamantinum" in thesis 9 is read as semicolon and may be a comma. Thesis 5 has a decorative initial "A" joined to "d". The line "Abauctoritate" in the source is transcribed as two words. Lines 3 through 9 are shown as printed; the list-like lines under 5 are set as <l>.
